record_identity.title: Claude-assisted GTG-50029 campaign breached European political and media targets and exfiltrated sensitive data

incident_identity.historical_event_name: Anthropic GTG-50029 European political-target cyber campaign
incident_identity.date_basis: Anthropic describes the campaign as occurring in spring 2026 and publishes associated actor-infrastructure observations spanning 6 February through 4 July 2026. The range is an outer bound for evidenced campaign infrastructure, not a claim of continuous intrusion activity.

summary: Anthropic reported that a single French-speaking actor used Claude and an agentic multi-agent workflow to target European political parties, media organizations, think tanks and their SaaS providers. Across 42 tracked entities, the actor obtained internal access to at least 14, exfiltrated an estimated 12 to 26 GB of database dumps, and extracted approximately 140,000 records containing users' political opinions from one compromised political-campaign management platform. Other stolen material included donor and membership records, a 15,000-message mailbox, student application records including data from minors, payment-provider data, and credentials. Anthropic also reported per-victim encrypted archives staged on an actor-run Tor leak site.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: Anthropic's September 2026 threat-intelligence report directly describes GTG-50029, including Claude-enabled agentic tooling, exploit development, at least 14 compromises among 42 tracked targets, approximately 140,000 political-opinion records from one campaign platform, and an estimated 12 to 26 GB of stolen data. Le Monde independently reported the same Anthropic-disclosed campaign and its concentration among French far-right organizations.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The occurrence demonstrates material AI-enabled offensive cyber uplift: one actor used agentic coding, parallel sub-agents and AI-assisted exploit development to increase the speed, breadth and operational depth of a multi-target intrusion campaign. The public evidence does not isolate a single current VIGIL system-failure mechanism with sufficient specificity, so the Incident is admitted without forcing a taxonomy classification.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: The campaign shows that frontier-model assistance can compress the labour and skill required for reconnaissance, exploit development, persistence, credential theft, data processing and multi-victim campaign management. Cyber governance therefore needs trajectory-level and cross-session controls rather than only local request filtering.
assessment_boundaries: Anthropic controls the underlying service telemetry; complete prompts, model traces, victim logs and exfiltrated datasets are not public.
The exact actor identity and complete victim list are not established in the reviewed public evidence.
Anthropic states that Claude Haiku, Sonnet and Opus were used across the cyber-operation cases in the report, but does not allocate every model version to every GTG-50029 action.
VIGIL does not determine criminal or civil liability or notification status for each affected organization.
The Incident is intentionally unclassified because malicious use and cyber uplift alone do not establish a specific current VIGIL failure class.

severity_assessment.materialised_consequence: The campaign obtained internal access to at least 14 organizations and exfiltrated an estimated 12 to 26 GB of data. One compromised political-campaign platform yielded approximately 140,000 records containing political opinions; other stolen material included donor and membership data, a 15,000-message mailbox, student application data including records involving minors, payment-provider data, and credentials. Exfiltrated archives were staged on an actor-operated Tor leak site.
severity_assessment.affected_scope: At least 14 compromised entities among 42 tracked European political, media, think-tank and SaaS targets, plus an unquantified population represented in the stolen records. The public evidence does not establish the total number of distinct affected individuals.
severity_assessment.seriousness_and_persistence: The incident produced substantial privacy, confidentiality and security harm across multiple organizations, including theft of special-category political-opinion data and persistent exposure risk from staged leak archives and credential interception. Full downstream dissemination and remediation status are not public, so permanence cannot be established.
severity_assessment.quantitative_information: Anthropic reports at least 14 internally compromised targets out of 42 tracked entities, approximately 140,000 political-opinion records from one campaign platform, an estimated 12 to 26 GB of database dumps, and one 15,000-message mailbox. Total affected-person count, financial loss, remediation cost and confirmed downstream leak consumption are not established.
severity_assessment.evidentiary_limits: Anthropic's threat-intelligence report is the primary technical source; VIGIL does not possess raw provider telemetry, victim logs or exfiltrated datasets. Exact actor identity, complete victim list, legal findings, total affected-person count and downstream use of every stolen dataset remain unresolved.
severity_assessment.band_rationale: S2 rather than S3 is supported because the campaign caused substantial realized multi-organization compromise and exfiltration of large volumes of sensitive data, including political opinions, credentials and records involving minors, with persistent exposure risk. S2 rather than S1 is appropriate because the reviewed evidence does not establish death, grave physical injury, severe child-safety harm, catastrophic critical-asset loss or comparably grave and enduring societal harm.
